releases.summary: Bio pages: one page with all your links, for your Instagram, TikTok or any other bio.

sections.title: Links
items: Bio pages: make a page at hrva.cc/@yourname with your name, a short bio, an emoji or initials avatar and a button for each of your short links. Pick a colour and a light, dark or automatic theme, reorder buttons by dragging or with the keyboard, hide one without deleting it, and see a live preview as you edit.

Every button is one of your own short links, so each click gets the same safety checks as any other link. A link that stops working, is blocked or is waiting for review disappears from your page, and the editor shows why.
Share your page with a copy-link button or a QR code from the Bio page screen.
When you share your page in a chat or on social media, its preview image shows your name, your @handle and your initials in your colour.

sections.title: Analytics
items: A Bio page view on the Analytics page shows views per day and, for each button, clicks that came from hrva.cc pages and all clicks on its link.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Bio page views are counted once per visitor per day with the same daily-changing one-way hash as link statistics. No IP address or browser details are stored, and the page loads no third-party scripts, fonts or trackers.
Search engines are asked not to list your page unless you turn on "Allow search engines to index this page".

sections.title: Link Safety
items: Anyone can report a bio page with "Report this page" at the bottom of it, or on the Report a link page with hrva.cc/@name.

sections.title: Admin
items: Bio pages: search pages by handle, name or owner, hide a page with a reason, and change or revoke a handle. A revoked handle is added to the reserved aliases.

Reports, and text that looks like impersonation or phishing, put a bio page in the review queue with Looks fine and Hide page. Discord hears about new bio page reviews and reports, and the daily decisions email counts them.
The stats page shows how many bio pages there are and how many views they had.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains bio pages step by step, linked from the Bio page screen and the Help center.

releases.summary: QR scans in link analytics, a public page with hrva.cc in numbers, a weekly summary and phishing-wave alerts for the admin, and the AI connector is sign-in only.

sections.title: Analytics
items: QR codes made by hrva.cc now count their scans: link analytics and the admin stats split clicks into QR scans and other clicks. Codes made before this release count as other clicks, so download a new code to count scans from it.

sections.title: Site
items: hrva.cc in numbers: a public page with site-wide totals for the last 30 days, such as active links, clicks per day, harmful links blocked and how fast reports are reviewed. It never shows anything about a single link or person.
A new help page explains the public numbers and QR scans, linked from both and from the Help page.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: The AI connector without an account (hrva.cc/mcp/anon) is gone. Connect hrva.cc/mcp and sign in instead.

sections.title: Admin
items: Weekly summary: every Monday morning, Discord and email get last week's clicks, visitors, bot share, new links and users, reviews and automatic blocks, the top 5 links, and how many reviews are waiting right now. Clicks, new links and new users are compared with the week before. Discord and email can be turned off separately.

Phishing-wave alert: Discord warns when 5 or more new links to the same new or unknown domain appear within an hour from at least 2 different accounts or networks, with a link to those links. Nothing is blocked automatically.
All URLs opens with a search from its address, so the alert's link lands on the matching links.

sections.title: Privacy
items: The public numbers page stores nothing about you beyond a rate-limit counter for your network, which expires after an hour. QR scans are a daily count per link, like the other link statistics.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Discord alerts for the admin show links, domains, reasons and visitor details in full instead of cutting them off with "…". Alerts that don't fit in one message are counted as "and N more".
Searching links, users or the review queue for % or _ now finds those characters instead of matching everything.
Searching links for a domain finds it in either spelling, such as čokolada.hr and xn--okolada-i6a.hr.
A web address whose domain name is longer than 253 characters, the most a domain name can have, is now refused as not a valid web address.
Signing in again from an admin page brings you back to the page you opened.
The report and unavailable pages no longer show the footer twice.
Password managers no longer offer to fill your username into a passkey's name.

releases.summary: Passkeys and security keys, and two-step verification for every sign-in method.

sections.title: Security
items: Sign in with a passkey: your fingerprint, face or screen lock, a password manager such as Bitwarden, Proton Pass or 1Password, or a security key such as a YubiKey. No password to type.
Add as many passkeys and security keys as you like in Settings, and rename or remove them there. You get an email whenever one is added.
Two-step verification can use a passkey or security key instead of a code, and can be turned on with passkeys only.
Google and GitHub sign-ins now ask for your second step when two-step verification is on, and accounts that use Google or GitHub can turn it on.
Recovery and authenticator codes work however you type them, with or without spaces, dashes or capitals.
Sign-in messages now say how many tries are left and when you can try again.
Deleting an account that signs in with Google or GitHub needs a sign-in within the last 15 minutes, as adding or removing a passkey does.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Passkeys store only a public key and a few details, such as the name you give it, when it was added and last used, and whether it's synced. Your fingerprint, face and PIN never leave your device.

sections.title: Site
items: A new help page explains passkeys and security keys step by step, linked from Settings and the footer.

releases.summary: Campaign tracking tags for your links, a full statistics page and reserved short link names for the admin, and a simpler admin menu.

sections.title: Links
items: Campaign tracking (UTM): when you create or edit a link, add Source, Medium and Campaign tags in a few clicks, with a preview of the final link. Your analytics tool reads them; hrva.cc doesn't.

sections.title: Analytics
items: Link analytics shows the full destination's campaign tags (UTM) when the link has them.

sections.title: Admin
items: Stats: one page with Traffic, Links, Users, Safety and System tabs for the last 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. It shows clicks and visitors across all links, top links and referrers, links created per day and how they were made, sign-ups, the review queue and blocks, and the server's health.
Long values are shown in full and wrap, instead of being cut off with "…".
The stats are totals only. Unique visitors are counted per link per day and added up, and nothing identifies a visitor.
Reserved aliases: keep short link names back, each with a reason. Nobody can create a link with one, random links never pick one, and links that already use one keep working.
New links remember how they were made: on the website, with an API key, in bulk or through the AI connector, with or without an account.
The admin pages have their own sidebar, grouped into Overview, Moderation, Content and Logs, in place of one long menu.
The dashboard's redirect timing, request count, cache hit ratio, app version and database and Redis status now show real values.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Admin pages show times in your own time zone.
Removing a reserved alias or a domain rule keeps keyboard focus on the list.
Look-alike links that mix alphabets, such as a Cyrillic letter in a well-known brand, are now caught and sent for review.
If an admin blocks a whole domain or several links at once, each owner now gets one email listing their blocked links instead of one email per link.
Sign-up refuses an email address that's too long before sending any email.

releases.summary: Fixes for reactivating links, addresses with accented letters, admin link edits and blocklist refreshes.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Reactivating a link works again, including when an admin unblocks a blocked link.
Links to addresses with accented letters, such as čokolada.hr, now redirect.
Older links whose address contains curly braces now redirect instead of showing an error.
When an admin changes a link's destination, the old destination's redirect details no longer come back, and a block made at the same moment is kept.
A refused link edit, such as an expiry date in the past, is no longer saved anyway.
Refreshing a blocklist source no longer undoes a change another admin made during the download, such as turning it off.

releases.summary: Fixes for long links and for two people picking the same short link name.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Links whose destination is longer than 255 characters no longer fail. Destinations can be up to 2048 characters, and longer ones get a clear message.
If two people pick the same custom short link name at the same moment, the second now gets "This short URL is already taken. Try another." instead of an error.
Bulk creation now answers an invalid link with a clear message instead of a server error.

releases.summary: Small fixes: header links when signed in, an accurate AI connector page and an up-to-date changelog.

sections.title: Fixes
items: The Features and API links in the header now work when you're signed in: the home page shows those sections below your shorten form.
The AI connector page no longer lists the no-account server, which can't create links while anonymous link creation is turned off.
This changelog covers everything since May again.

sections.title: Site
items: Blog posts and the privacy and terms pages link to the author's site, karlo.cc.

releases.summary: Privacy-first link analytics with referrers, countries and devices, plus Discord alerts and bulk review for the admin.

sections.title: Analytics
items: Rebuilt analytics for each link: clicks per day, daily unique visitors and bot clicks, with its top referrers, countries, devices, browsers and operating systems.
Rebuilt analytics overview across all your links, with a daily trend and your top 10 links by clicks.
Pick a range of 7, 30, 90 or 365 days. Times are shown in your own time zone.
Bots, link previews and crawlers, including the check Outlook runs before it opens a link, are counted separately and never as clicks or visits.
Bots and link previews can no longer use up a visit-limited link: they aren't sent to its destination.
A link's visit count now counts each person once per day and leaves bots out.
Daily statistics start on 24 October 2026. Earlier clicks are included only in a link's all-time visit count.

sections.title: Privacy
items: Link statistics are daily totals per link. Nothing is recorded about an individual click, and IP addresses are never stored for link statistics.

To count unique visitors, the IP address and browser identifier are combined with the link and a random key that changes every day into a one-way hash. The hashes and the key are kept only in Redis, never in the database, and expire a few hours after the day ends, so a visitor can't be followed across days or links.
The country comes from Cloudflare, which carries hrva.cc's traffic; hrva.cc doesn't look up locations itself.
The old visit records, which held a hashed IP address for each visitor, have been deleted.
The privacy policy and the home page describe the new daily statistics.

sections.title: AI Connector
items: link_stats now takes a range of 7, 30, 90 or 365 days and shows a link's top referrers, countries and devices, next to its clicks, daily unique visitors and bot clicks.

sections.title: Admin
items: Discord alerts: hrva.cc posts to the admin's Discord channel when a link is flagged for review or reported by a visitor, when a link is blocked automatically, when someone signs up, and when a blocklist fails to load or loads again. Alerts are sent together every 30 seconds and never include email or IP addresses.
Review queue: select up to 100 entries and resolve them in one go. A domain they share is blocked or trusted once for all of them.
Audit log: every entry has a readable action name, failed actions are marked, and the log can be filtered by action.

releases.summary: Layered checks against phishing and malware, a page for reporting links, and a review queue for doubtful ones.

sections.title: Link Safety
sections.description: hrva.cc now checks where links lead when they're created, every night, and on every click.
items: New links are checked against public blocklists of harmful domains and exact links (HaGeZi, OpenPhish, PhishTank, URLhaus and Phishing.Database). hrva.cc downloads the lists to its own server and refreshes them regularly, so checking a link against them sends it nowhere.
hrva.cc also checks how old a destination's domain is, looks it up in the Spamhaus domain blocklist, and watches for names that imitate well-known brands or pose as login pages.
A destination known to be harmful can't be shortened. A doubtful one is saved and sent to a person for review instead of being blocked.
After a link is created, hrva.cc follows its redirects in the background and checks every address along the way.
Every night, all active links are checked again against Google Safe Browsing and the latest lists.
Every click is checked against the blocking lists first. A link whose destination has been listed since it was created stops working on that click.
If one of your links is blocked, you get an email. If a whole account is blocked, its owner gets a single email.

sections.title: Reports & Unavailable Links
items: Anyone can report a hrva.cc link for phishing, malware, spam or other abuse on the new Report a link page. Reports go to a person for review and never block a link on their own.

A short link that doesn't work now opens a page saying why: it was disabled for leading to a harmful site, it expired, it reached its visit limit, its owner turned it off, or it doesn't exist. The page has a button to report the link.
hrva.cc publishes its abuse contact, abuse@hrva.cc, at hrva.cc/.well-known/security.txt.

sections.title: Blog & Policies
items: New blog post: How hrva.cc stops phishing links. It covers the scam links found in September, what hrva.cc checks now, and what it still can't catch.
The privacy policy and terms of use have new sections on how links are checked, reported and moderated, and on which services see a destination's domain or URL.

sections.title: Admin
items: Blocklists page: add, edit and refresh list sources, each with fallback mirrors and its own refresh interval; see each list's size and last error; manage Block and Allow rules for domains; and test any URL to see every check that matches it.
Review queue for flagged and reported links, with Looks fine, Trust domain, Block link, Block domain and Block user. The admin menu shows how many entries are waiting.

Blocking a domain switches off every active link to it and its subdomains at once. Trusting a domain clears its reviews and, after checking them again, restores its links that a blocklist, scam signals or a domain rule had blocked.
Blocking a user deactivates the account and blocks its links; unblocking restores both, after a confirmation that names the user.
All URLs shows why a link was blocked, and domains and users can be blocked straight from the table.
Accounts that behave like typical scam accounts are marked as possible scammers, with a filter on the Users page. The marker never blocks anything by itself.

The daily admin email became a decisions email: it's sent only when something needs a decision and lists open reviews, automatic blocks, possible scammers and failing lists, without the text visitors wrote.

Admins can moderate from Claude or ChatGPT through the AI connector: read the review queue and possible scammers, check a URL, block links, domains and users, and delete links. These tools can't unblock or trust anything and won't change more than 50 links at once. Deleting a link, blocking a domain or blocking a user needs a flag or block from the automatic checks first, since a visitor report alone isn't enough. Users appear only as masked email addresses.

releases.summary: Fixes from a security scan, working email sign-up, an hourly limit on new links, and admin tools for spotting abuse.

sections.title: Security
items: Account details returned by the API, including the response to a password reset, no longer include the password hash.
Previews, QR codes and other public lookups of a short link no longer show the owner's email or tags, and keep a password-protected link's destination hidden until it's unlocked.
Wrong passwords on protected links are rate limited, and wrong two-factor codes count against the account.
Setting up two-factor authentication again no longer switches off the one that's already active.
A custom alias stays taken after its link expires or is turned off, so nobody else can claim it.
Link previews never fetch private or internal network addresses, on any redirect.
New passwords need at least 8 characters.
Link passwords are no longer written to the admin audit log, and older entries were cleaned up.

sections.title: Links
items: Each account can create up to 60 links an hour, across the website, API keys and AI apps. Every link in a bulk upload counts.
Links to other URL shorteners, or back to hrva.cc, are refused. Share links such as t.co, lnkd.in and Google's share links still work.
You can reactivate links you turned off yourself.
The nightly Safe Browsing check no longer skips links, and a link it blocks can't be reactivated by its owner.
Reactivating a link checks it with Safe Browsing again and makes sure no other link holds its alias.
Short links keep working when the cache is down, and a link stops as soon as it reaches its visit limit.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Signing up with email and password works again. The form now confirms the sign-up and shows what to fix in each field instead of "Request failed".
Reminder emails for links that are about to expire are sent again.
Signing in or out clears data left over from the previous session, and a network error no longer signs you out.
Deleting the last link on the last page goes back a page, and selecting links for a bulk action only picks the ones on the page you see.
Check a link says when a link is password protected instead of showing an empty destination.
Settings shows your sign-in email as read-only, instead of an email form that couldn't save.

sections.title: Admin
items: Resend failed emails from the email log. Emails stuck sending for 10 minutes are marked failed, and stored email content is deleted once it's sent, or after 7 days if sending failed.
All URLs: search by owner email or a pasted hrva.cc/abc link, show anonymous links only, sort by owner, and see a Suspicious marker with its reasons. The delete button works again.

Suspicious-link flags for lookalike brand names, login lures, high-risk domain endings, dynamic DNS hosts, raw IP addresses, punycode and chained shorteners. They only flag; nothing is switched off automatically.
A daily email lists new links from accounts younger than a week and links flagged as suspicious.
Audit log entries list only the fields that were sent, show a password as changed or removed, and label failed actions clearly.
Editing an API key's limits works again, and the health page reports email delivery from the latest email.

releases.summary: Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps to your hrva.cc account.

sections.title: AI Connector (MCP)
sections.description: hrva.cc now has an MCP server at hrva.cc/mcp.
items: Connect Claude (web, desktop and phone), Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or another MCP app that supports remote servers with sign-in, and it can shorten links into your account, list them and check their visits.
The app signs in through hrva.cc: you log in as usual, with your password and two-factor code or with Google, then allow or deny the app on a consent page.
Links an AI app creates are tagged "ai".
Settings → Connected apps lists each connected app with when it was first connected and last used. Disconnecting an app cuts off its access at once.
New MCP server page with setup steps for each app.
The privacy policy explains what is stored for connected apps and for how long.

sections.title: Links & Sign-in
items: A destination must be a real web address: http or https with a proper domain name. Anything else gets a clear error instead of becoming a broken link. A bare domain such as example.com still gets https:// added.
Signing in takes you back to the page you were trying to open.

sections.title: Security
items: Fixed a gap that let a signed-in user edit a link they didn't own. Only a link's owner or an admin can edit it now.

sections.title: Admin
items: Admins can change where a short link points. The new destination is checked with Google Safe Browsing first.

releases.summary: A new look, a new logo, and privacy and terms pages.

sections.title: Redesign
items: A fresh, modern design across the site, with a new logo and a cleaner light theme. Dark mode is still there and follows your system setting.
Every public page now shares the same header and footer.
The dashboard, admin pages, blog and changelog were restyled to match.

sections.title: Privacy & Terms
items: New Privacy Policy and Terms of Use pages, linked from the footer.
hrva.cc is a non-commercial hobby project of HrvaLabs, and the footer, privacy policy and terms link to the HrvaLabs website.

sections.title: Fixes
items: The home page fits on narrow phones, and the footer links wrap onto a new line instead of running off the screen.

releases.summary: Email verification, two-factor auth, account self-service, analytics, and URL tags.

sections.title: Accounts & Security
items: Email verification on registration — new accounts must confirm their email before signing in (existing users grandfathered, Google accounts auto-verified).
Two-factor authentication (TOTP) for password accounts, with one-time recovery codes and a second login step.
Account active status now enforced everywhere: deactivated users are blocked at login and per-request.
Self-service account deletion (password-confirmed) that removes the user and all their URLs and API keys.
Deactivating a user now revokes their API keys; an API key works only while both the key and its owner are active.

sections.title: URLs & Analytics
items: Password-protected links — lock a short URL behind a password (registered users); visitors enter it before the redirect resolves.
URL tags — organize links with tags, filter by tag, see them on the dashboard.
Per-URL and overview click analytics (visits, unique recent visitors, new-visitor trend).
URL and API-key status now shows the real reason: Active, Expired, Limit reached, Revoked, Deactivated, or Blocked.
Customizable QR codes — pick colors, size, and error-correction level, with PNG and SVG download.

sections.title: Admin & Privacy
items: Download-my-data export (profile, URLs, API keys, emails) as JSON.
Admin gets notified by email when a new user registers; dashboard shows new-user counts (7d / 30d).
Admin-only endpoints are hidden from the public API docs.

releases.summary: URL creation reliability, clearer errors, hardened validation.

sections.title: URL Creation Fixes
sections.description: Bare domains and pasted whitespace no longer break URL creation.
items: Auto-prepend https:// when the scheme is missing (e.g. test.gmail.com → https://test.gmail.com).
Trim leading/trailing whitespace on submitted URLs.
Persist-time validation failures now return 400 with a field-level error instead of 500.
Friendlier, end-user-oriented validation messages across the API.

sections.title: Routing & Safety Hardening
items: Reserved-word check for custom short URLs now matches exactly (case-insensitive) instead of prefix-match, so loginpage and apifoo are valid again.
Expanded reserved list: api, login, logout, oauth2, actuator, error, swagger-ui, v3, webjars, auth.
Bot probes (.env, favicon.ico, robots.txt, wp-login.php, etc.) return 404 silently — no log, no DB hit, no metric.
Custom short URL alias validated against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$ with 32-char cap.
Safe Browsing failures now log loudly with ALERT prefix; new app.safe-browsing-fail-closed flag to fail-closed when the API is unreachable.

sections.title: Auth & Config
items: Removed GitHub as an OAuth2 SSO provider. Google remains.
Short URL generation now uses RandomStringUtils.secureStrong() (SecureRandom) instead of the deprecated Math.random()-backed API.
OAuth2 user creation now persists once with active=true instead of INSERT + UPDATE.
app.google-api.key now bound to GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_KEY env var.

releases.summary: Search & filter your links, refined UX, better testing.

sections.title: URL & User Search / Filtering
sections.description: Find your links faster with powerful filters.
items: Dashboard: search input filters by long URL and short URL keywords.
Status dropdown (All / Active / Inactive) toggles visibility of deactivated links.
"Expired only" checkbox shows only links past their expiration date.
Date range pickers (dateFrom / dateTo) filter by creation date.
Admin users page: search by email and filter by active status.
Admin URLs page: search, status filter, expired-only checkbox, and sortable columns (Visits, Created).
Backend uses JPA Specifications for composable, dynamic queries.
Filter params bundled into UrlSearchDto / UserSearchDto instead of scattered @RequestParam annotations.

sections.title: Pagination Overhaul
items: Pagination bar is always visible — even on single-page results.
New "Showing X–Y of Z" total element count so you know the full scope.
Page size selector (10/20/50/100) with disabled prev/next buttons when at boundaries.
Applied to both dashboard (URLs) and admin (users) tables.

sections.title: Landing Page UX
items: Removed "Show advanced options" toggle from public hero form — custom alias, visit limit, and expiration silently didn't work for anonymous users. Now the form is dead-simple: paste URL → Shorten.
Logged-in form now shows alias, limit, and expiry directly without a toggle. Power users see the options immediately.
Hero subtitle updated to: "Shorten links in seconds. Sign up free for custom aliases, visit limits, expiration dates & analytics."
After shortening a link as anonymous user, a subtle upsell card appears: "Create a free account to set custom aliases, visit limits, and track analytics."
Status page link (status.hrva.cc) restored in footer — was lost in the React migration.
Footer now sticks to bottom of viewport using flex-1 layout.

sections.title: Sortable Columns
items: Dashboard: Visits, Created, and Expires columns are clickable with arrow indicators (↑↓↕).
Admin users: Email, Created, Last Login, and Status headers are sortable.
Admin URLs: Visits and Created columns are sortable.
Sort state persists in URL params (?sort=visits&order=asc) across page refreshes.
Default sort: URLs by newest first (createDate,desc), users by ID ascending.

sections.title: Admin URL Management
sections.description: Admins can now fully manage all URLs in the system.
items: Activate/deactivate toggle for any URL — deactivated URLs show a ToggleLeft icon to reactivate.
Edit dialog to change visit limit and expiration date on any URL.
New PATCH /api/v1/urls/{id}/activate endpoint on the backend.
Admin URLs page now has search, status filter, expired-only checkbox, and pagination with total count.
Row entrance animations and copy pulse on the admin URLs page.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
items: Double scrollbar bug: removed overflow-x-hidden from root container — CSS spec was forcing overflow-y: auto, creating a nested scroll container.
Blur decorative elements now properly clipped with overflow-hidden on their section parents.
URL count on landing page stats bar now uses totalElements instead of content.length — showed wrong count when user had more than 20 URLs.
Deactivate toggle icon changed from ToggleLeft (ambiguous "off" position) to ToggleRight (clearly shows active URL can be turned off).

sections.title: Animations
items: Copy button pulse: brief scale bump (1→1.25→1) on copy for tactile feedback.
Staggered row entrance: table rows fade in one by one with 30-40ms delays.
Stats counter: landing page totals tick up from 0 with ease-out animation.
Filter cross-fade: table remounts on filter change, re-triggering entrance animation.

sections.title: Easter Eggs
items: Konami code (↑↑↓↓←→←→BA) — turns the page into a rainbow overlay for 5 seconds.
/fortune page — random URL-themed fortunes that refresh on each visit.
/egg page — a duck that quacks. Quack it 10 times for a surprise QR code.
Console message — opens dev tools to find a hint. ✨
Changelog footer — the see-no-evil monkey wiggles on hover.

sections.title: Admin Tools
sections.description: New admin capabilities for system management.
items: Audit Log table — every admin action (deactivate/activate/delete/update) is auto-logged with timestamp, admin email, and details via AOP aspect. Paginated view at /admin/audit-log.
Email Log table — all sent emails recorded with SENDING/SENT/FAILED status tracking. View delivery status at /admin/email-log.
System Health page — green/red status indicators for Database, Redis Cache, SMTP, and SafeBrowsing API.
Login Rate Limits viewer on admin dashboard — shows active IP rate limits with auto-refresh and clear-all button.
Bulk URL Management — checkbox selection on All URLs table with batch Activate/Deactivate/Delete actions.
New admin nav links: Health, Audit Log, Email Log.

sections.title: Cache Improvements
items: Redirect endpoint now cache-first: every GET /{short} checks Redis before DB, with validation on cache hit.
Cache warmup on startup: top 20 most visited, most recent, and recently accessed URLs pre-loaded into Redis.
Cache priming on creation: newly created URLs immediately cached.
TTL increased from 60 minutes to 7 days (stale data caught by validation on cache hit).
SafeBrowsing recheck scheduled task: daily at 2 AM, re-scans all active URLs against Google SafeBrowsing. Flagged URLs auto-deactivated and owner notified via email.

sections.title: Tests
items: 6 new unit tests for URL and User filtering (search, active, expired, date range).
2 new tests for URL activate endpoint and service method.
Updated existing tests to match new service and controller signatures.
3 new tests for scheduled safe browsing recheck and audit wiring.
Total: 150 tests, all passing (JUnit 5 + Mockito).

releases.summary: Complete frontend rewrite from Angular to React (Next.js). OAuth2 login, URL expiry notifications, performance overhaul.

sections.title: Frontend: Angular → React Rewrite
items: Complete rewrite from Angular to Next.js (React 19, App Router).
Server-side rendering for faster initial page loads and better SEO.
Dark/light theme toggle using next-themes with system preference detection.
Fully responsive layout optimized for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
Radix UI primitives with custom design system (glassmorphism cards, amber accent).
Animated page transitions with CSS keyframes (fade-up, scale-in).

sections.title: URL Management
items: Dashboard with full URL table: sort, search, filter, paginate.
Inline URL shortening from the landing page (anonymous).
Advanced shortening dialog with custom alias, visit limit, expiration date.
Per-row actions: copy short URL, open original, QR code modal, analytics modal.
Bulk URL creation via API keys.
CSV export of your URLs.
QR code generation (PNG, configurable size).
Link preview endpoint (Open Graph metadata: title, description, og:image).

sections.title: Authentication & Accounts
items: Registration with email/password validation.
Login with JWT token-based auth, stored in localStorage.
Password reset flow (request → email → confirm).
Account settings page with password change.
OAuth2 login with Google and GitHub (spring-boot-starter-oauth2-client).
OAuth2 users automatically created on first login; email locked to provider.
Login attempt rate limiting (20 attempts/day per IP).

sections.title: Dashboard & Analytics
items: Per-link analytics with visit count, progress bar (vs visit limit).
Dashboard stats: total URLs, total visits, active API keys.
Recent links sidebar on landing page (5 most recent).
"View all" link to full dashboard.
URL deactivation and permanent deletion with confirmation dialogs.

sections.title: API Key Management
items: Generate, revoke, and manage API keys.
API key usage tracking (calls used / limit).
Expiration dates on API keys.
X-Api-Key header support for programmatic access.

sections.title: Admin Panel
items: Admin dashboard with system stats (total URLs, users, visits, cache status, uptime).
User management: edit email, API key slots, active status.
User deletion with confirmation.
Server metrics: JVM memory, Java version, active profiles, request count.

sections.title: Backend: Performance Overhaul
items: Read-only transactions (@Transactional(readOnly = true)) at class level on all services.
Redis caching with 60-min TTL on URL peek lookups; graceful degradation on Redis outage.
Migrated from Gradle to Maven for faster builds and simpler configuration.
Java 21 + Spring Boot 3.x upgrade.
Removed unused beans, exceptions, and tests (code cleanup).
OAuth2 URL configuration via environment variables.
Default CORS configuration.

sections.title: Scheduled Tasks
items: URL expiry notifications: daily at 8 AM, emails users about URLs expiring within 24 hours.
URL deactivation: every minute, deactivates expired URLs.
API key deactivation: every hour, expires old API keys.
User deactivation: daily at 10 AM, disables unused accounts after configurable inactivity period.
IP cleanup: every minute, removes old IP address records.
Reset token cleanup: every minute, deactivates expired password reset tokens.

sections.title: Security & Compliance
items: Google Safe Browsing API v4 integration — every URL checked before shortening.
JWT stateless authentication with configurable secret and expiry.
Client IP resolver with ForwardedHeaderFilter support (works behind proxies).
Actuator endpoints: /actuator/health public, all others ROLE_ADMIN only.
CORS configured for frontend origin + standard HTTP methods.

sections.title: Infrastructure
items: Docker multi-arch builds (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64).
GitHub Actions CI: build → test → Docker push to ghcr.io on main branch.
PRs trigger build-only (no push).
Docker Compose for local development (Postgres + Redis + MailHog).
Individual Dockerfiles for flexible deployment.
Portainer environment variables for OAuth2 secrets.

sections.title: Tests
items: 140+ unit tests across controllers, services, validators, converters, and models.
JUnit 5 + Mockito + AssertJ test stack.
No Testcontainers, no @ActiveProfiles, no test slicing — all pure Mockito unit tests.

Expiration dates (link expires at specific time).
Link analytics with per-URL visit tracking.
Dashboard for managing all your shortened URLs.
User registration and authentication.
Password reset via email.
API key generation and management.
QR code generation for any short URL.
Admin user management (CRUD, activate/deactivate).

sections.title: Tech Stack
items: Angular 14+ frontend with Material Design components.
Spring Boot 3.x backend with Spring Data JPA.
PostgreSQL database with Liquibase migrations.
Redis caching layer.
Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.
Docker deployment on Heroku.
